sections.title: Annual herb
sections.text: Summer savory is an annual of the mint family, usually around 10–50 cm tall. Its much-branched stems carry narrow aromatic leaves; the plate shows the fine foliage and pinkish-white flowers.

sections.title: Leaves and flowers
sections.text: Leaves are typically linear to lance-shaped and roughly 1–5 cm long. Small, two-lipped flowers grow in whorls along the upper stems in summer.

sections.title: Culinary use
sections.text: The aromatic leaves are used as a culinary herb. The species is distinct from perennial winter savory (Satureja montana), despite their related names.
